recommended_architecture: External systems produce files, forms, analytics exports, CRM exports, client system exports, SHS system records, ClientOps records, report usage records, manual verified entries, approval workflow records, API exports, or webhook-style future records
SHS Direct Connect V1 stores local connector registry, connection status, mapping previews, sync-run previews, and audit events
Direct Connect evaluates connector payloads through Adapter, Batch Import, Event/Webhook, API Gateway, Warehouse Sync as applicable
Verified Aggregation, Audit & Verification, Data Approval, Reports, Watchtower, and ClientOps consume only readiness metadata until records pass governance
No credentials, OAuth exchange, bank account connection, live banking feeds, external calls, production persistence, public approval, or SHF Impact mutation in V1

placement_decision.reason: The repo already formalizes the required architectural neighbors as layers. Direct Connect should bind connector setup/status to those layers instead of duplicating them.

risks: Financial-data connectors require stronger privacy, consent, credential, and audit controls than current V1 scaffolds provide
Existing import UI is mock/client-facing and should not be mistaken for backend readiness
Older sync/webhook utilities can call or simulate sends and must not bypass V1 no-external-send rules
localStorage is appropriate for V1 mock state but not production connection or credential persistence
Reports can overstate trust if connector-fed source readiness is not tied back to Truth Spine and Data Approval
